title: John Robichaux's band and radio work; Zutty Singleton and Red Happy
summary: He lists the Robichaux band's men, its radio stock-music work, and drummers at the Lyric Theater.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Well, this band, this band stretched on out to, let's see, uh, Robeshoe Band, that's right. John Robeshoe Band. John Robeshoe Band.
Who was in that at that time?

Let's see, John Robeshoe Band, we had, let's see, now we had Old Man McCurtis, he's dead, Willie Humphrey, George Augustine on bass, Mercedes Goldman on piano, and we had, let's see, John, you see, was playing banjo with John Robeshoe. And then we had, sometimes Willie Paglia was to play trumpet. Uh-huh. And we had, uh, Charlie Love, John Robeshoe, himself on the band, on the violin, and Harrison Bones on trombone. Oh, yeah. I was on the drum, I'm thinking we played banjo, John, care banjo player sometimes. You know, Professor John Robeshoe, in terms of... Was that a radio band, you know?
Was that a radio all the time? Yeah, it was all stock music. And if it was in between, use music and then fake some of them, you know. Uh-huh. It was like a pure own band, it was a radio band.
That was before Alec Bigard worked with him, was it or after? Oh, it might have been after.

Because I was the first man when the Earl Roachhoe Band went in the field. He was the first man went in that band, but he was using the, let's see, he played a while with it. But that's when he come out from the Lyric Theater. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah, he was doing the most field spot work. During the time of the Lyric Theater, well, he had Happy. Happy played the longest because he had a drummer named it called Zooty Singleton.

Zooty, yeah. Zooty played a good while with him in the show. Uh-huh. And then, uh, they were starting around, right after World War I, 1920, 21, like that. Then Zooty went away. Happy came in that band. That was a regular show drummer. Yeah. Red Happy.
Oh, yeah, Red Happy. Red Happy.
Black Happy. No, Red Happy. Yeah. No, not Black Happy.
